findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, so it receives a routable public endpoint reachable from outside the VPC. Combined with a default-master username of "admin", this materially increases the attack surface for brute force and exploitation of the MySQL listener.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the MySQL database, its automated storage, snapshots, and logs unencrypted. Anyone obtaining the underlying storage or a snapshot can read the data in cleartext.

The policy attached to the EC2-assumable role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*". Any code running on the instance (or an attacker who compromises it) obtains full control of S3, EC2, and RDS account-wide, including the ability to escalate privileges, exfiltrate all buckets, and delete databases.

The DB password (var.password), username, endpoint, and database name are embedded in cleartext into the instance user_data script and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. user_data is readable via the instance metadata service and the console, and the resulting PHP include file exposes live database credentials on the web server.

MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR (${aws_vpc.portal_vpc.cidr_block}) rather than to the application security group. On a publicly accessible database this permits any host in the VPC — including non-application workloads — to reach the database listener on the standard port.

The database security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This allows a compromised or maliciously configured database host unrestricted outbound connectivity, enabling data exfiltration and callbacks to external command-and-control infrastructure.

The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = ON, so clients can connect to the database over unencrypted transport. Credentials and query results can be transmitted in cleartext across the network to the publicly reachable endpoint.
